# thwip

> Commit-carried CI evidence for agent-run pipelines. Run CI on the machine
> where the code lives, sign a compact proof of the exact Git tree, and let a
> ruleset-protected GitHub check verify it in seconds. The merge queue merges
> on that proof; nothing reruns in the cloud.

thwip is a control plane, not a CI compute platform. Evidence is a single git
trailer (`thwip-Proof: v1.<base64url DSSE envelope>`) over an in-toto
Statement v1 with predicate `urn:thwip:attestation:ci-run:v1`, signed with a
dedicated OpenSSH key enrolled to the author's device. Verification derives
all repository facts from GitHub, fetches one signed fact bundle from the
control plane, and fails closed with stable reason codes (PASS,
SUBJECT_TREE_MISMATCH, SIGNER_KEY_REVOKED, ...).

Security profiles per project: fast (signed local proof), remote (GitHub runs
every required check), fresh (the queue signs an assignment, your machine
runs the suites and signs a receipt naming what ran and against what tree,
and the control plane checks the receipt against the assignment), and audited
(fresh plus that same run repeated in GitHub Actions, with the merge waiting
on both verdicts).

What a proof establishes, stated precisely: who ran the approved checks, on
exactly which Git tree, under which policy version, signed by a key enrolled
to a GitHub account that currently holds repository permission. thwip does not
observe execution and never sees source code. False claims are detected by
reproducibility rather than surveillance: identical inputs produce identical
digests on every machine, so a fabricated claim disagrees with teammates'
runs, later commits, and any cloud run, permanently and attributably. The
remote profile is SLSA Build L3 (GitHub builds and signs the provenance); fast
is an attributed assertion plus the hermeticity, reproducibility, and
two-party controls that SLSA's original L4 specified and v1.0 dropped.

## Install

The CLI is published on npm as `@recallnet/thwip`. The installed command is
`thwip`; there is no repository to clone.

    npm install -g @recallnet/thwip     # or: npx @recallnet/thwip
    thwip login
    thwip init --required "lint,typecheck,test"
    thwip run

Node 22 or newer.

## Pages

- [FAQ](https://thwip.recall.net/faq.md): profiles, membership, commit
  signing, rebases, data handling
- [Developer setup](https://thwip.recall.net/install.md): agent prompt for
  preparing a machine — install the CLI, device-flow sign-in, and register an
  ed25519 signing key with GitHub. Also printed by `thwip setup`.
  Repository setup is a separate prompt, on each project's dashboard page.
- [Dashboard](https://thwip.recall.net/dashboard): GitHub-mirrored org
  management (requires sign-in)
- [Blog](https://thwip.recall.net/blog/): product announcements and guides
- [RSS](https://thwip.recall.net/rss.xml): blog feed

## Blog

- [Verifiable agent coding](https://thwip.recall.net/blog/beta.md): research
  note on edge-signed commit-carried CI evidence, trust bounds, and open
  invitations
- HTML: https://thwip.recall.net/blog/beta/

## Facts

- Membership and permissions come from the GitHub organization; there are no
  invitations. Verification checks current GitHub permission.
- Project settings inherit organization defaults from the dashboard. A
  committed thwip.yaml can partially override them after protected merge.
- The thwip GitHub App evaluates exact PR heads and publishes the thwip check;
  observe mode runs it under a separate name first. A branch
  running Thwip Queue requires that context from whoever publishes it: GitHub
  Actions while the repository observes, satisfied by the thwip-required.yml
  workflow setup adds, and the App once an administrator enforces.
- Thwip Queue performs the merge from the control plane on the App's contents
  write, composing the commit on the base it verified and moving the branch
  without force. There is no repository merge workflow or branch-write secret.
- Plans: Free (3 projects, 5 signers), Pro $5/month or $50/year (15 projects,
  25 signers). Both verify identically.
